harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 18 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on Alpine Linux 3.23. All replication traffic is carried over TLS 1.3 and restricted to peers presenting a certificate issued by a cluster-dedicated CA (mutual TLS, clientcert=verify-full). All three nodes were then individually restarted (native reboot, one at a time, standbys first then primary), with boot identity, service health, and replication/data verified both before and after each restart.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql18 (+contrib, +openrc) on node1, node2, node3 via apk
Generated a dedicated cluster CA (ca.key/ca.crt) on node1 under /etc/postgresql-ca
Issued CA-signed server certs for node1/node2/node3 (CN=hostname, SAN=DNS+IP) and a CA-signed client cert for role 'replicator'

Repaired locked root accounts on node2/node3 (passwd -u root) to enable cluster-keypair SSH, then distributed CA cert, node certs, and replicator cert/key via scp; set ownership postgres:postgres and permissions (600 keys, 644 certs, 755 dir)

initdb'd node1 as primary; configured postgresql.conf (ssl=on, ssl_cert/key/ca_file, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, hot_standby) and pg_hba.conf (hostssl replication replicator <standby-ip>/32 cert clientcert=verify-full, plus hostnossl reject-all fallback)
Created REPLICATION LOGIN role 'replicator' on node1
Verified cert enforcement: connection from an unauthorized IP rejected, connection without a client cert rejected, connection with a rogue non-CA-signed cert rejected

Ran pg_basebackup -R over TLS (verify-full, client cert) from node2 and node3 against node1, auto-populating primary_conninfo with TLS/cert settings; configured matching postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf on each standby; started both standbys
Verified streaming replication via pg_stat_replication/pg_stat_ssl on node1 (TLSv1.3, client_dn=/CN=replicator) and confirmed pg_is_in_recovery()=t on standbys plus data propagation via a test table
Enabled postgresql in the default OpenRC runlevel on all three nodes
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, service status, replication state, row counts) on all nodes
Rebooted node2, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified postgres started, standby recovery, and reconnection to primary as a TLS streaming replica
Rebooted node3 following the same sequence and verified the same recovery evidence

Rebooted node1 (primary) last, confirmed changed boot_id, verified pg_is_in_recovery()=f (writable primary), pre-existing data intact, both standbys reconnected via TLSv1.3 with client cert, and a new write on node1 propagated to node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured across node1/node2/node3 with node1 as writable primary
evidence.summary: node1 initialized and started as primary; node2/node3 cloned via pg_basebackup -R and started as standbys; a row inserted on node1 was observed on both standbys and pg_is_in_recovery() confirmed the primary/standby roles

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a CA created for this cluster
evidence.summary: Cluster CA generated on node1; server/client certs issued from it; pg_stat_replication joined with pg_stat_ssl on node1 shows both standbys connected with ssl=t, version=TLSv1.3

evidence.requirement: Replication connections accepted only from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf restricted to hostssl ... cert clientcert=verify-full for the standby IPs only; connection attempts without a client cert, without TLS, from an unauthorized IP, and with a rogue non-CA-signed cert were all rejected; only connections presenting the CA-issued 'replicator' cert succeeded (client_dn=/CN=replicator)

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered primary + replication
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id ebcbf628... captured; reboot acknowledged (stream closed); post-reboot boot_id d31185e2... confirms restart; primary came back writable (pg_is_in_recovery=f) with prior data intact; both standbys reconnected via TLSv1.3 with CA-signed cert and received a new post-restart write

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered standby + replication
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 6262c375... captured; reboot acknowledged (stream closed); post-reboot boot_id 9f528f14... confirms restart; postgres auto-started via OpenRC runlevel, pg_is_in_recovery=t, prior data intact, and reconnected to node1 as a TLS streaming replica

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered standby + replication
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 0a089d8f... captured; reboot acknowledged (stream closed); post-reboot boot_id 026a6329... confirms restart; postgres auto-started via OpenRC runlevel, pg_is_in_recovery=t, prior data intact, and reconnected to node1 as a TLS streaming replica
